entities.summary:
Quintus Cornificius was a prominent Roman senator and orator from the gens Cornificia, who played a significant role in the Roman Republic during the late Republic period. He served as a general and an augur, and was known for his poetic and literary works, including the lost epyllion Glaucus. Cornificius was a close friend and correspondent of the famous Roman poet Catullus and the statesman Cicero. His significance lies in his contributions to Roman politics and literature, as well as his connections to influential figures of his time. 

 Born into a family of senatorial rank, Cornificius rose to prominence through his military and literary achievements. His writings provide valuable insights into the culture and politics of ancient Rome during this period. 

 As a general, Cornificius participated in several military campaigns, including those against the Germanic tribes and the Dacian Kingdom. His literary works, including his epyllion Glaucus, have been lost to time, but their influence can still be seen in later Roman poetry. 

 Cornificius's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his connections to other notable figures of the time, such as Catullus and Cicero, demonstrate his importance in Roman cultural and intellectual circles. His significance in the broader context of Roman history can be seen in the ongoing impact of his writings and the influence of his friendships and alliances on the development of Roman literature and politics. 

 Quintus Cornificius's story serves as a reminder of the enduring power of literature and politics to shape the course of human history. His life and works continue to fascinate scholars and historians, offering a unique window into the complexities and challenges of ancient Roman society.
